instruction: Using Visual Studio Code, create a Python script named `shark_fatality_risk_model.py` in the `/home/user/analysis_results/shark_attacks/` directory. The Kaggle dataset in that directory (Global Shark Attacks) contains a CSV file with incident records, including columns similar to `Fatal (Y/N)`, `Country`, `Activity`, `Sex`, and `Age`. In this script, load the main CSV file with pandas, remove rows with missing values in the `Fatal (Y/N)` column, and map `Fatal (Y/N)` to a binary target column `Fatal` where `Y` → 1 and all other values → 0. Select a feature set including encoded `Country`, `Activity`, `Sex`, and numeric `Age` (after filling missing ages with the median). One-hot encode the categorical features, then split the data into 75% training and 25% testing sets, stratifying by `Fatal`. Train a `RandomForestClassifier` with at least 200 trees. Compute `Precision`, `Recall`, `F1-score`, and `ROC-AUC` on the test set. Save the metrics to a text file named `shark_fatality_risk_metrics.txt` containing exactly one line formatted as: `Precision: <value>, Recall: <value>, F1: <value>, ROC_AUC: <value>`.
